independence_note: No prior candidates, strategy prompts or results were read.

case.valued_outcome: In a synthetic tabletop puzzle club, explain intermittent short-count returns well enough to choose a bounded change that keeps at least five complete twelve-counter kits available and reconciles each returned loan within five minutes of tray placement.

hard_constraints.text: Each loan requires exactly twelve counters in one numbered tray; an eleven-counter tray cannot be issued as a complete kit.
Investigation is limited to one additional twenty-minute club block with at most two volunteers and forty total volunteer-minutes.
Borrowers may use a kit for five minutes; an investigative change cannot shorten that allowance or interrupt a loan already in progress.
No counters may be purchased or permanently marked during the investigation; the counters remain visually indistinguishable.
The return area must remain usable throughout the block; no more than one tray may be held aside for inspection at a time.

observations.text: Stipulated synthetic starting record: one volunteer counted twelve counters in each of six numbered trays before three twenty-minute club blocks; no independent starting recount was recorded.
Stipulated synthetic loan log: eighteen loans were completed across the three blocks, with six loans per block and a five-minute use allowance.
Stipulated synthetic anomaly: four of the eighteen first return-shelf counts recorded eleven counters; three such counts occurred in the final two minutes of a block and one occurred near its middle.

Stipulated synthetic follow-up: within three minutes of each of three short counts, one loose counter was found on the shared intake mat and placed in the contemporaneous short tray, making its count twelve. No loose counter was found during the five-minute closing search following the fourth short count.
Stipulated synthetic evidence limit: the three found counters had no identifying marks, and nobody recorded their arrival on the mat, so the record does not establish which loan supplied them.
Stipulated synthetic tray record: tray one had two short counts, tray four had one, and tray six had one; every tray also had at least one recorded twelve-counter return.

Stipulated synthetic timing record: first shelf counts occurred zero to two minutes after placement, with times rounded to whole minutes; ten of the eighteen placements had no volunteer watching the transfer itself.

resources.text: Six existing shallow open trays, numbered one through six, are available for checkout, return, or one-at-a-time inspection.
Seventy-one counters are currently accounted for after closing; one counter remains unresolved, and there are no spare counters.
Two volunteers can attend the next twenty-minute block, providing at most forty person-minutes of observation and handling.
The existing shared intake mat, return shelf, and checkout table are available within the same small room.
One stopwatch and one paper tally sheet are available to record transfer times, counts, and tray numbers.
Six removable paper tray labels and one pencil are available; labels may identify trays but may not mark individual counters.
A camera, extra staff, replacement counters, and another investigation block are unavailable.

case.preferred_dependency: Prefer retaining the existing numbered open trays and self-service shelf return, because these let borrowers return kits without waiting for a volunteer; this preference may be reconsidered if evidence shows that the dependency prevents the valued outcome.
case.causal_return_path_hypothesis: Hypothesis H1: some borrowers place a final counter on the shared intake mat after placing their tray, so early counts capture a delayed return. Competing hypothesis H2: ordinary volunteer handling or borrower traffic shifts counters between trays and the mat, so later loose counters merely fill shortages from other loans. Competing hypothesis H3: some single-person starting or return counts are wrong. Directly observing transfer order and obtaining an independent count could discriminate among these hypotheses, but none is established by the stipulated record.

parent_operations.text: Assemble and issue a numbered tray with twelve counters, record its checkout time, and let the borrower use the kit for five minutes.
Receive the tray at the self-service return shelf, count its counters, and reconcile any shortage using the shared intake mat before making the kit available again.

available_observables.text: A volunteer can record the order and elapsed seconds of tray placement, loose-counter placement, and subsequent handling for transfers that the volunteer directly watches.
Two volunteers can separately count one selected tray before checkout or after return and record disagreement without assuming that either count is correct.
Counts of counters on the intake mat and in a selected tray can be recorded at placement and at fixed later times; visually identical counters cannot be linked to individual loans.
The tally can record active loans, waiting borrowers, tray number, and time remaining in the block, subject to the volunteers' finite attention.

unknowns.text: Whether the loose counters found after short counts came from the corresponding borrowers, another active loan, or volunteer handling is unknown.
The accuracy of the unrepeated starting and return counts is unknown; the existing log provides no independent count check.
The location of the unresolved counter and whether closing-time concentration reflects transfer delay, handling congestion, counting error, or chance are unknown.

ordinary_archive.operation: Considered ordinary operation: ask a second volunteer to recount a short tray immediately before any counter is added.
ordinary_archive.relation: A recount addresses the hypothesis that the apparent shortage is a return-count error and uses the existing counting step.
ordinary_archive.probe: For a selected short return, record both counts separately, then check whether disagreement persists on a joint count.
ordinary_archive.limits: Agreement cannot establish that the starting kit had twelve counters or identify where a missing counter went; recounting also consumes volunteer attention.

ordinary_archive.operation: Considered ordinary operation: hold a short tray aside for up to three minutes and inspect the intake mat at fixed intervals.
ordinary_archive.relation: A short waiting period addresses the hypothesis that the final counter arrives after the tray and extends the existing reconciliation step.
ordinary_archive.probe: Record the tray and mat counts at placement, one minute, and three minutes, together with any directly witnessed counter placements.
ordinary_archive.limits: An unobserved loose counter cannot be attributed to the loan; holding one tray reduces immediate availability, and a three-minute wait cannot settle permanent loss.

ordinary_archive.operation: Considered ordinary operation: give borrowers a brief reminder to place all twelve counters inside their numbered tray when returning it.
ordinary_archive.relation: The reminder addresses the hypothesis that return instructions permit delayed or separate counter placement while retaining self-service returns.
ordinary_archive.probe: During the bounded block, record reminder delivery, directly observed transfer order where feasible, and first-count shortages.
ordinary_archive.limits: A change in shortage frequency in one small block could reflect attention, traffic, or chance; a reminder alone does not distinguish handling shifts from counting error.
